detail: ran 20 s without crashing, 50 frames/s, free heap 391916 -> 391916
finalText:
Done. The board now keeps sending indefinitely.

## Root cause

`main/link.h` documents the ownership contract: on `ESP_OK` the link takes ownership of `pkt->data` and frees it; **on any error the caller keeps ownership and must free it**.

`send_with_retry()` in `main/main.c` called `encode_frame()` (a `malloc(len + 8)` = 4104 bytes) on every attempt, but only the success path released the buffer. When the simulated radio returned `ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT` (1 in 5 calls, plus queue-full), the buffer was never freed — a ~4 KB leak per failed attempt.

At 50 Hz with ~20% failures that is ~52 KB/s of lost heap. The serial stats showed it exactly:

```
stats seq=0   ... retries=0  heap_free=391916
stats seq=250 ... retries=62 heap_free=129524
stats seq=350 ... retries=87 heap_free=23056
stats seq=400 sent=360 retries=90 failed=41 heap_free=14088
... sent=360 frozen, failed growing +50 every second
```

Once heap was exhausted, `encode_frame()` returned `NULL` on every iteration, so `send_with_retry()` bailed out with `ESP_ERR_NO_MEM` before ever retrying — every send failed forever.

## Fix

One change in `main/main.c`, honoring the link's documented ownership rule:

```c
esp_err_t err = link_send(&pkt);
if (err == ESP_OK) {
    return ESP_OK;
}
/* link_send only takes ownership on ESP_OK; free the packet on failure. */
free(pkt.data);
ESP_LOGW(TAG, "send failed (%s), retrying", esp_err_to_name(err));
retries++;
```

`link.c`, `link.h`, the frame size, and the 50 Hz rate are untouched.

## Verification

Clean rebuild (`rm -rf build`) and reflash; captured over 60+ seconds:

```
stats seq=0    sent=1    retries=0   failed=0 heap_free=391916
stats seq=1950 sent=1951 retries=487 failed=0 heap_free=391916
stats seq=3000 sent=3001 retries=750 failed=0 heap_free=391916
```

`heap_free` is flat, `sent` tracks `seq`, `failed` stays 0 — the occasional `ESP_ERR_TIMEOUT` retries happen as designed and no memory is lost.
